candidates.title: Impact Properties of Metal Fan Containment Materials Being Evaluated for the HSCT
observed_facts: NASA describes metal specimens impacted by projectiles of various sizes and shapes at speeds up to 350 m/s, at room or elevated temperature.
The visually inspected article page contains a penetration-velocity versus areal-weight graph for four anonymized materials at 370 C.
The cited NTRS record 20050171018 exposes no downloadable file; the same one-page article is available inside NASA compendium 19960041413.
official_model_results: NASA states that a dynamic finite-element program was used to guide testing and containment-system design, but publishes no deck or numerical model definition on the article page.

authoritative_primary_provenance.reason: NASA primary institutional record and government report.

lawful_open_access_and_license.reason: The report is public-use government work, but no model file or reusable model-file license exists in the record.

bounded_downloadable_deck_or_reconstruct.reason: No deck, geometry, material identities, mesh, contacts or complete projectile definition are published.

failure_and_regularization_complete.reason: Post-test metallography is mentioned, but no numerical failure law, parameters or objective regularization are supplied.

measured_validation_outputs.reason: The graph has units but anonymizes materials and omits the projectile definition and complete test conditions needed for deterministic validation.

mesh_and_convergence_definition.reason: No mesh levels, convergence observable or numerical uncertainty study is reported.

local_execution_feasible_and_bounded.reason: No executable or reconstructible model is available for a bounded local run.

contradictions_and_unknowns: The article establishes a relevant experimental regime but not a reproducible benchmark case.

candidates.title: Transient Finite Element Analyses Developed to Model Fan Containment Impact Events
observed_facts: NASA reports UDRI tests on 20 by 40 inch contoured metal panels impacted obliquely by a fan-blade root section.
The two-page article identifies DYNA3D, kinematic hardening, Cowper-Symonds rate dependence and an effective-plastic-strain failure criterion.
The authors varied maximum effective plastic strain to obtain good qualitative agreement and state that accurate parameter-determination methods still had to be established.
official_model_results: The article states that penetration velocity and impact deflection compared well, without publishing numerical series or uncertainty.

authoritative_primary_provenance.reason: NASA primary institutional record and government article.

lawful_open_access_and_license.reason: The article is public-use government work, but no solver model file or model-file reuse terms are supplied.

bounded_downloadable_deck_or_reconstruct.reason: The article omits the complete geometry, mesh, boundary conditions, contacts, material parameters and deck.

failure_and_regularization_complete.reason: Maximum effective plastic strain was varied for qualitative agreement; no fixed calibrated value, fracture energy or characteristic-length treatment is given.

measured_validation_outputs.reason: Penetration velocity and deflection are described only qualitatively; no measured time history or numeric validation table is published.

mesh_and_convergence_definition.reason: No mesh sequence or convergence/uncertainty result is published.

local_execution_feasible_and_bounded.reason: The legacy DYNA3D deck and a documented local conversion route are absent.

contradictions_and_unknowns: The source explicitly characterizes the comparison as qualitative and the predictive material parameters as unresolved.

candidates.title: Development of a Generic Gas-Turbine Engine Fan Blade-Out Full-Fan Rig Model
observed_facts: The FAA report is a 100-page primary government report, DOI 10.21949/k25w-vn45, using LS-DYNA 971R4.

It reports two casing through-thickness meshes with a 3 percent change in maximum casing strain energy, and three non-nested blade mesh configurations whose predicted fragmentation changes with refinement.
The report states that failure strain required event-, mesh-, stress-state- and strain-rate-dependent tuning and that blade breakup remained sensitive to in-plane element size.
The official repository exposes one PDF and no solver deck; full-model runtimes reported in the document range from 10 to 208 hours on 8 to 24 processors.
official_model_results: The model reproduced a qualitative event sequence and damage zones consistent with industry-reported tests and public literature, but the report does not publish a paired measured force, impulse or residual-velocity dataset for the modeled full-fan rig.
The third, finest blade mesh changed the qualitative outcome from partial tearing to fragmentation; this is sensitivity evidence, not convergence.

authoritative_primary_provenance.reason: FAA primary report in the USDOT ROSA P repository with DOI and report number.

lawful_open_access_and_license.reason: The report is publicly readable, but the repository supplies no model file with explicit reuse terms.

bounded_downloadable_deck_or_reconstruct.reason: No LS-DYNA deck or complete CAD/mesh definition is listed, and the full rig cannot be deterministically reconstructed from report figures alone.

failure_and_regularization_complete.reason: Johnson-Cook and constant-strain deletion are documented, but the report explicitly finds mesh/event-dependent tuning and supplies no objective damage-energy or characteristic-length regularization.

measured_validation_outputs.reason: Consistency with reported FBO tests is qualitative; no paired measured time history or fully specified quantitative rig-test comparator is exposed.

mesh_and_convergence_definition.reason: Three blade meshes are not a nested convergence sequence and change the fragmentation result; only two casing thickness meshes are compared for strain energy.

local_execution_feasible_and_bounded.reason: The required proprietary LS-DYNA deck is absent and reported full-model runtimes greatly exceed the 60-minute-per-mesh ceiling.

contradictions_and_unknowns: The report is a strong method and sensitivity comparator, but its own mesh and failure findings prevent treating it as a converged validation benchmark.

candidates.title: Altair RD-E 2602 Ductile Failure Model - ruptured plate
observed_facts: The official example uses a rigid sphere to perforate a metallic circular plate and compares Johnson-Cook, TAB1 and BIQUAD failure formulations.
The documentation declares a 77,961-byte input ZIP and the normalized official URL returned HTTP 200 during a bounded HEAD check; V9K did not download it.
The example states that strain-rate and thermoplastic effects are omitted and deletes shell elements after a damage or integration-point criterion is met.
official_model_results: The published results compare numerical failure treatments and deletion options; no physical experiment or measured validation series is shown.

lawful_open_access_and_license.reason: The files are publicly downloadable, but the inspected page states All Rights Reserved and no explicit reusable deck license was identified.

bounded_downloadable_deck_or_reconstruct.reason: The official page declares a small downloadable input ZIP for the complete example.

failure_and_regularization_complete.reason: Failure parameters and deletion options are shown, but no characteristic length, nonlocal formulation or objective fracture-energy regularization is documented.

measured_validation_outputs.reason: The example is a numerical feature demonstration with no experimental measurement comparator.

mesh_and_convergence_definition.reason: No three-level mesh study or declared converged impact observable is supplied.

local_execution_feasible_and_bounded.reason: The small official Radioss example is compatible with the installed OpenRadioss solver and is expected to be bounded, although V9K does not execute it.

contradictions_and_unknowns: Executable solver example status does not make this a physical validation case, and the projectile remains rigid.
